entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Borrows a form of government to describe a manner; the comparison is the insult.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Implies the boast is invented as well as unwelcome.

entries.definition: contented to a fault with oneself or one's actions
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Contentment that should have been alarm - the danger was there to be seen.
examples: he had become complacent after years of success

entries.definition: below average in quality or performance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The broadest word in English doing narrow work: below average, and nothing more.

entries.definition: resembling swine; coarsely gluttonous or greedy
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same comparison, and the commoner of the two insults.

entries.definition: (of persons or their actions) able or disposed to inflict pain or suffering
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Plain and physical, and the least ornamented of the strong words.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Turns critical the moment the object does not deserve it - glorifies violence is the usual company it keeps.

entries.definition: in the manner of a beast
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *bestial*: denies the person's humanity outright, which is why it is reserved for atrocity.

entries.definition: openly distrustful and unwilling to confide
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and wary rather than hostile; it expects a trick, not a betrayal.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The boasting is empty and long-winded - the complaint is about the volume.

entries.definition: not having enough money to pay for necessities
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Absolute and vivid - not a coin left.

entries.definition: offensively self-assured or given to exercising usually unwarranted power
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Power exercised alone, and answerable to nobody.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt slang accusation of cowardice.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Rare and studied. Whether that is praise depends on how hard the search shows.

entries.definition: befitting a monk; inclined to self-denial
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Self-denial by vocation, and slightly mocking when applied outside a monastery.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *wealthy*: substantial and settled money - more dignified than 'rich'.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The same picture, rarer and slightly more comic.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Cheer that resists being pushed down; the metaphor is a thing that will not sink.

entries.definition: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British slang, jokey and dismissive.

entries.definition: apprehending and responding with speed and sensitivity
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises speed of understanding rather than depth.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *brave*: the plain, universal praise - facing what frightens you.
examples: bravely he went into the burning house

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Strong condemnation, common enough to have lost some of its force.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *beautiful*: the full word - unreserved and applicable to anything from a face to an argument.
examples: her face was beautifully made up

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Often affectionate about films and pop songs; the badness is part of the appeal.

entries.definition: concealing crafty designs for advancing your own interest
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The furthest word here: plotting as an ongoing occupation.

entries.definition: characteristic of those having an inflated idea of their own importance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The literal compound, and neutral enough to be reclaimed as self-care.

entries.definition: having or marked by unusual and impressive intelligence
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Exceptional intelligence - the strongest ordinary compliment.
examples: a brilliant solution to the problem

entries.definition: filled or scattered with a disorderly accumulation of objects or rubbish
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: About too many things rather than dirt; a cluttered desk can still be working.
examples: his library was a cluttered room with piles of books on every chair

entries.definition: without pity; in a merciless manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *remorseless*: adds the aftermath: there was no regret once it was done.

entries.definition: make off with belongings of others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Deliberately grand for a small crime - often used in jest.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: An invitation to look at something ridiculous; the judgement is on the thing, not the looking.
examples: Get a load of this pretty woman!

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Unflattering - the skeleton showing through.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *grubby*: mild enough to be affectionate about a child, and mildly damning about a motive.

entries.definition: very thin especially from disease or hunger or cold
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Literary and grim - thin to the point of resembling a corpse.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Small, quick and stinging - it describes the remarks more than the mood.
examples: witty and waspish about his colleagues

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Curiosity with the wonder still in it, and no agenda attached.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Latinate and cool - it is the species name doing double duty.
examples: a source of valuable insights and sapient advice to educators

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *dreadful*: emphatic disapproval with a formal, slightly literary edge.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The most extreme word here, and it casts the target as a victim rather than a culprit.
examples: The critics crucified the author for plagiarizing a famous passage

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *sincere*: the plain claim that there is no gap between what is felt and what is said.
examples: she praised him sincerely for his victory

entries.definition: showing or motivated by sympathy and understanding and generosity
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Locates the kindness in the character, and forgives clumsiness in carrying it out.

entries.definition: lacking refinement or cultivation or taste
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Coarseness with class in it - the offence is against taste as much as manners.
examples: appealing to the vulgar taste for violence
the vulgar display of the newly rich

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *cantankerous*: difficult by habit rather than by temper; the contrariness is settled, almost fond.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *tricky*: has drifted to describing problems rather than people; of a person it is still a warning.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Old-fashioned scorn from a theory that pale organs meant no courage.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The spaced spelling, older and slightly more formal.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Chiefly American; blowing one's own horn, with the same air of hot air.

entries.definition: appropriate (as property entrusted to one's care) fraudulently to one's own use
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Theft by someone trusted with the money - the betrayal is what makes it grave.
examples: The accountant embezzled thousands of dollars while working for the wealthy family
The treasurer embezzled from the charity for years.
